purpose: Compare the local effects of deleting an entire older source frame against the already frozen random 1024-key deletions on the same raw-window reads. This is an exploratory follow-up after inspecting the random-group results, not an independent preregistered validation.
selection: Use the identical target reads and eligibility rule as lean_utility_group_deletion_v1. Require exactly five attributed older sources of 1024 spatial keys each, exclude conditioning, newest source and all unattributed keys. Sort sources chronologically and remove one entire source per arm, preserving all other keys, positions and pointers. If five sources do not match these conditions, exclude the read. No labels determine membership.
controls: Each of the five source arms removes 1024 keys, as do the previously frozen random-group arms. Keep the full read as an unmatched-key no-op reference. Compare local effects and per-read ranges; do not infer a significance test from overlapping arms. Use exactly the same labels, masks, reads, checkpoint and video states as the preceding study.
verification: Reuse the source provenance and fixed-read no-op checks, repeat every replay in two fresh processes, independently verify source-group membership, key counts and masks, and independently rescore masks after predictions are frozen. Report excluded reads and empty-frame false alarms separately.
limits: A local source deletion is conditional on all other memory keys and attention renormalization. Large effects do not establish a better propagation strategy or individual token utility. The follow-up was motivated by prior results; the existing split is sequence-separated with unknown patient independence. No labels enter inference, and no redetection or new confidence gate is introduced.
